items.longBusinessSummary: Alphabet Inc. offers various products and platforms in the United States, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, the Asia-Pacific, Canada, and Latin America. It operates through Google Services, Google Cloud, and Other Bets segments. The Google Services segment provides products and services, including ads, Android, Chrome, devices, Gmail, Google Drive, Google Maps, Google Photos, Google Play, Search, and YouTube. It is also involved in the sale of apps and in-app purchases and digital content in Google Play and YouTube; and devices, as well as the provision of YouTube consumer subscription services, such as YouTube TV, YouTube Music and Premium, NFL Sunday Ticket, and Google One. The Google Cloud segment offers consumption-based fees and subscriptions for AI solutions, including AI infrastructure, Vertex AI platform, and Gemini enterprise. It also provides cybersecurity, and data and analytics services; Google Workspace that include cloud-based communication and collaboration tools for enterprises, such as Calendar, Gmail, Docs, Drive, and Meet; and other enterprise services. The Other Bets segment sells transportation and internet services. Alphabet Inc. was incorporated in 1998 and is headquartered in Mountain View, California.

Title: OuterBox Connects Its Proprietary Lead Tracking to Google Ads, HubSpot, and Salesforce
Author: OuterBox   Tue, October 27, 2026 at 1:00 PM GMT+1 3 min read
Published: 2026-10-27T12:00:00+00:00
=== BODY ===
COPLEY, OH / ACCESS Newswire / October 27, 2026 / OuterBox, a full-service performance marketing agency, today announced integrations between LOOP Analytics, its proprietary lead tracking platform, and Google Ads and CRMs like HubSpot and Salesforce. The platform now shows clients which Google Ads campaigns deliver actual revenue, not just form fills. A paid search click that turns into a signed contract six months later now shows up in reporting as revenue, connected to the exact campaign and keyword that brought it in.
"If you've ever wondered whether your marketing spend is actually working or just filling up a report nobody reads, that's the exact question LOOP is built to answer," said Matt Prater, EVP of Innovation at OuterBox. "Real leads, tied to real revenue, tied to the campaign that actually earned it."
Revenue credit from the CRM: When a deal closes in HubSpot or Salesforce, the revenue flows back to LOOP in real time and attaches to the campaign and keyword that produced the lead, even months later. Marketing and sales finally work from the same numbers, and LOOP never writes to the client's CRM. More CRM platform integrations are coming soon.
"LOOP lets us connect the dots and find the gaps in a client's strategy," said Jordan Sen, Group Director of Integrated Strategy at OuterBox. "Whether that's a missing page or a keyword gap, we can identify it and act in real time."
Development moved faster through the Additive Tech Fund, a Google partnership that funds technology built to plug into how advertisers already run their campaigns. For clients, that means LOOP works inside their existing Google Ads accounts. OuterBox built LOOP and continues to run it.
"The direction is clear," said Prater. "Less time digging through dashboards, more time acting on what the data is already telling you."
OuterBox clients can access the upgrades now, and some features come with specific service packages.
Learn more about LOOP Analytics, including a walkthrough video, at https://www.outerboxdesign.com/digital-marketing-services/analytics/loop/.
OuterBox is a full-service performance marketing and web development agency helping businesses grow through SEO, paid media, conversion rate optimization, email marketing, and web design and development. Founded in 2004 and headquartered in Copley, Ohio, OuterBox pairs specialized, industry-focused teams with a unified operational structure and 20+ years of proven expertise.

=== META ===
Title: Earnings live updates: SoFi stock surges on 'exceptional' quarter, raised outlook
Author: Yahoo Finance     Updated Tue, October 27, 2026 at 1:22 PM GMT+1 1 min read
Published: 2026-10-27T12:22:24+00:00
=== BODY ===
Third quarter earnings season is in full swing this week, with corporate results on deck from Big Tech heavy-hitters Microsoft (MSFT), Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL), and Amazon (AMZN).
Aside from Big Tech, industries from oil to chips to pharmaceuticals will be represented, as Exxon Mobil (XOM), Intel (INTC), Boeing (BA), Ford (F), and Eli Lilly (LLY) also open their books.
It's shaping up to be another strong earnings season. According to FactSet data, nearly a quarter of S&P 500 companies have already reported Q3 earnings so far, with an overall earnings growth rate of 29.5%. If that rate holds, it will mark the third straight quarter of earnings growth above 25%.
SoFi (SOFI) stock surged 10% in premarket trading on Tuesday after the online financial services provider lifted its 2026 outlook and reported strong results for the third quarter.
Here's what SoFi reported for Q3, compared to Wall Street analyst estimates compiled by S&P Market Intelligence:
Revenue: up 45.9% year over year to $1.39 billion, above estimates of $1.26 billion.
Adjusted earnings: $0.18, above estimates of $0.17.
Updated 2026 guidance: SoFi now expects net revenue of $5.04 billion in 2026, reflecting a 40% year-over-year increase. Adjusted EBITDA is now expected at $1.66 billion of adjusted EBITDA, and earnings per share are forecast at $0.61. Wall Street analysts were expecting 2026 earnings per share of $0.59.
The company also introduced 2027 guidance, guiding for $0.90 of earnings per share, which is above the Street's estimate of $ 0.82.
"We had exceptional Q3 results against the backdrop of any environment, but they are even more remarkable given how 2026 has unfolded," CEO Anthony Noto said. "Our focus is simple. We are adding more members, who are using more products, and generating more revenue per product to create the most value for our shareholders over the long run. In less than a decade, we have transformed SoFi from a single-product company into an everything financial app with eight different businesses each generating over $100 million in annualized revenue."
Whirlpool posted another mixed quarter as inflation and lower demand in North America took a toll.
"What is new and different is the increasingly inflationary environment that has happened from Q2 into Q3, as well as the impact of volume deleveraging which is driven by the softer demand that we have in the North America industry," Whirlpool CFO Roxanne Warner told Yahoo Finance, adding that the team is focusing on what it can control.
In the third quarter, the company reported revenue declined by nearly 9% to $3.68 billion, which was below estimates of $3.91 billion. The company reported an adjusted loss per share of $0.21, lower than the adjusted earnings per share estimate of $0.76, per Bloomberg consensus data
Warner said that the industry hasn't caught up to the "full impact of the inflationary pressures from 2022," with inflation up 12% since then.
For that reason, the company plans to raise prices for the third time this year, now by 7% in the fourth quarter. That follows its largest price increase in history in April, at 10%, and a 4% increase in its list prices in July.
Revenue for major appliances in its North America business fell 8.3% year over year to $2.5 billion, below Wall Street's expectations.
Whirlpool's small domestic appliance business fell almost 1% to $286 million, below the expected $314 million. However, the company said that in the third quarter, some items sold out, leading to roughly 40% year-over-year growth in US orders in October.
items.summary: Third quarter earnings season is in full swing this week, with corporate results on deck from Big Tech heavy-hitters Microsoft (MSFT), Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL), and Amazon (AMZN).

Title: Anthropic’s Founders Will Keep Control With a Single Share of Stock
Author: Omor Ibne Ehsan   Tue, October 27, 2026 at 1:21 PM GMT+1 5 min read
Published: 2026-10-27T12:21:19+00:00
=== BODY ===
Amazon booked $53 billion in Q2 pre-tax income primarily from Anthropic, and Alphabet recorded a $99 billion gain, yet both hold nonvoting Class N stock with zero say in governance.
Unlike Zuckerberg's individual 60.8% vote grip on Meta, Anthropic's seven founders collectively share 50.1% voting power on roughly 10% combined economic ownership.
Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and Google didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat GOOG. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.
On October 26, 2026, Anthropic filed its public Form S-1. The private maker of Claude seeks a Nasdaq Global Select listing of Class A stock under the proposed symbol ANT. The filing's most important term involves a single share of Class F stock.
Just before the offering, Anthropic will issue a single share of Class F stock to Anthropic Founders, LLC, whose initial members are its seven co-founders. That share carries 50.1% of total voting power, and the filing states it "will not have any economic rights."
The filing leaves the price range and share count blank. The filing does not mention a reported valuation of $1.5 trillion to $1.75 trillion.
Until ANT trades, listed exposure runs through Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG, NASDAQ:GOOGL), which fell 1.06% to $316.80, and Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), which rose 0.44% to $249.09. Both hold nonvoting Class N stock, so they own economics without a vote.
Class A voting power is capped at 49.9%, and Class F power is not diluted by future issuances. The founders therefore decide elections of non-trust directors, certain charter amendments, and any merger or sale.
Board control is split. The Long-Term Benefit Trust elects four of seven directors through one Class T share, while Class F and Class A together elect the other three.
24/7 Wall St has helped investors make money for over two decades, and our top analysts just finished ranking the definitive Top 10 Stocks To Buy Now. Not the ten biggest companies. Not the ten everyone is arguing about. The ten best stocks to buy right now.
The report is free, and you can see why we think each stock is a top investment today.
Inside the LLC, each founder gets one vote and a simple majority rules, and in a deadlock, the share votes in proportion to Class A votes cast.
The filing explains the arrangement this way: "We believe that our seven co-founders... as a group, are distinctly equipped to be stewards of our mission."
Each original founder may suggest a ranked list of up to ten replacements, effective once five of the other six approve while all seven remain. Those lists "shall be strictly confidential and shall not be publicly disclosed by any Member or the Company."
The first eight designees must meet residency rules and hold three years of tenure at Anthropic or a nonprofit or public-benefit group. The ninth and tenth slots carry no such requirement.
A founder remains a member by keeping at least 2% of IPO-date Class A holdings. One could thus give away 98% of a stake and still vote.
Replacements can join only until the offering's tenth anniversary. If fewer than three founders remain for 90 consecutive days, a 450-day transition begins, after which the Class F share is redeemed for no consideration.
Mark Zuckerberg holds 60.8% voting control of Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) on about 14% of the economics. Anthropic's version is collective and fixed, and outside estimates put the seven founders at about 10% combined ownership.
Anthropic already shows up in both income statements. Amazon booked $53.40 billion of second-quarter pre-tax other income "primarily from investments in Anthropic," and Alphabet's quarter included a $99.03 billion gain on equity securities.
Those are paper marks set against market values of $3.92 trillion and $2.69 trillion. The voting design changes little for either company, because nonvoting holders were never going to control Anthropic.
The bigger risk is that the structure "may make us ineligible for inclusion in indices," which could keep index funds out and pressure the valuation behind those marks.
In the bull case, Anthropic's first-half revenue reached $16.29 billion, up from $1.16 billion a year earlier, and most of its $80.7 billion net loss was a $72.4 billion non-cash fair-value change.
The bear case centers on governance. Class A buyers "generally will not be able to affect the outcome of any matter submitted to a vote of our stockholders," and insiders may sell 10% of locked-up shares from the first trading day.
At launch, AI IPOs built this way likely warrant a visible governance discount, and investors researching them can check whether the offering price reflects one. Alphabet, by comparison, trades at a P/E of 14 while Google Cloud revenue grew 82% in the second quarter.
The amended S-1 will be the test: if its price range implies a valuation near the reported top with these terms unchanged, the discount is missing. Alphabet's report, expected October 28, will show how large its Anthropic mark has become.
If you have cash sitting in your account right now, give this two minutes. After more than two decades of helping investors beat the market, our top analysts at 24/7 Wall St. put together a definitive report on the Top 10 Stocks To Buy Today. And GOOG wasn't one of them.
